title: What is the difference between arrow functions and regular functions?
description: Understand this binding and function syntax differences.

data.text: **Question:** What is the difference between arrow functions and regular functions?

Arrow functions have lexical this binding, cannot be used as constructors, have no prototype property, and have a shorter syntax. Regular functions have their own this context, can be used with new, and have a prototype.

**Arrow Functions:**
- Lexical this (inherits from enclosing scope)
- Cannot be used with new (no constructor)
- No prototype property
- No arguments object
- Shorter syntax

**Regular Functions:**
- Dynamic this (depends on how called)
- Can be used with new
- Has prototype property
- Has arguments object
- Can be used as methods

data.takeaway: Arrow functions are great for callbacks, but use regular functions when you need dynamic this or constructor behavior.
